memory_candidates.content: When an extension adds a context file under a NEW tier directory (e.g. context/patterns/ in an extension whose manifest declares only project/<domain> entries), the file never propagates: loader.lua's M.copy_category is driven by manifest provides.context, and check-extension-docs.sh enforces both directions -- line 236-240 fails a declared entry missing on disk, and Rule L reports a deployed context file tracing to no provides.context entry. EXT_DIR defaults to $REPO_ROOT/agent-system/extensions, so these checks scan the SOURCE STORE and apply even to an extension with no .claude-extensions.json entry (undeployed). A top-level directory-name entry is the right shape (core already declares 'patterns'), and Rule L unions each extension's own files rather than overwriting, so multiple extensions may declare the same directory name. Ordering matters: create the directory/file FIRST, then append to provides.context, so no intermediate state is red. Any plan that adds a context file under a new tier therefore has a file set of N+2 (manifest.json and index-entries.json), not N.
